caller_census.method: full .text byte scan for e8 rel32 calls and e9 rel32 jumps to 0x514be80; the scan also finds the recursive self-call at 0x514be97, which is recorded separately and is not a caller

callers.arg_setup: rdi = [rbx + 0x18] immediately before the call (the caller's own +0x18 link)

notes: Instruction-level detail lives only in the raw objdump excerpt; this JSON holds semantic records only.
This function has no endbr64: its first instruction is test %rdi,%rdi. The 7 int3 bytes after the ret are genuine padding to the next FDE at 0x514bee0.
objdump's nearest-symbol annotations are explicitly not claimed as symbol names; the delete stub's identity comes from its .rela.plt relocation, not from the annotation.
The qwords at node + 0x0 and node + 0x8 are never read by this function, so no role is claimed for them.
The callers' enclosing functions are not modelled here; only the four call sites and their immediate argument setups are recorded, and this packet claims the entry, not exclusive ownership of it.

The neighbouring function at 0x514bee0 is a different teardown variant (0x58 node size, different field offsets, a 0x514b690 destructor call) and is NOT claimed here; the following FDE at 0x514bf60 is likewise a separate item.

rule.arguments: rdi = node pointer (saved in rbx); void return
rule.loop: after the node delete, advance to the next link saved before disposal; stop when it is null
rule.null_input: a null input returns immediately with no frees
rule.per_node: for each node in the +0x10 chain, in order: (1) recursively tear down the +0x18 link, (2) dispose the string at +0x20, (3) delete the node with size 0x48
rule.string_disposal: if the string pointer at node + 0x20 equals node + 0x30 (the inline-buffer address) nothing is freed; otherwise operator delete (pointer, capacity + 1 mod 2**64) is called, where capacity is the qword at node + 0x30
